verses.text: "At that time," says the LORD, "I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be my people."
This is what the LORD says: "The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness. I will come to give Israel rest."
Long ago the LORD appeared to us and said: "I have loved you with a love that lasts forever. That is why I have kept drawing you to me with faithful love.
I will build you up again, and you will be rebuilt, young Israel. Once more you will pick up your tambourines and go out dancing with joy.
Once more you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria. The farmers will plant them and enjoy their fruit.
A day will come when watchmen on the hills of Ephraim will shout, 'Come, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!'"
This is what the LORD says: "Sing with joy for Jacob. Shout for the greatest of the nations. Make it known, praise, and say, 'LORD, save your people, the survivors of Israel!'

Look, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the ends of the earth. Among them will be the blind and the lame, pregnant women and women in labor. A huge crowd will come back.

They will come weeping, and I will lead them as they pray. I will guide them beside streams of water, on a smooth path where they will not stumble. For I am Israel's father, and Ephraim is my firstborn son.
Listen to the LORD's message, you nations. Announce it in the faraway coastlands. Say, 'The one who scattered Israel will gather them and watch over them like a shepherd watches his flock.'
For the LORD has rescued Jacob and set him free from someone too strong for him.

They will come and sing for joy on the heights of Zion. They will be radiant over the LORD's good gifts: the grain, the new wine, the olive oil, the young sheep and cattle. Their lives will be like a well-watered garden, and they will never be sad again.
Then young women will dance for joy, and young men and old men too. I will turn their mourning into joy. I will comfort them and give them gladness instead of sorrow.
I will give the priests more than enough, and my people will be filled with my good gifts," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted, because her children are gone."
This is what the LORD says: "Stop your crying and wipe away your tears, for your work will be rewarded," says the LORD. "Your children will come back from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your future," says the LORD. "Your children will come back to their own land.
I have clearly heard Ephraim mourning: 'You disciplined me, and I was disciplined like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will come back, for you are the LORD my God.
After I turned away, I was sorry. After I understood, I beat my chest in sorrow. I was ashamed and humiliated, because I carried the disgrace of my youth.'
Is Ephraim not my dear son, the child I delight in? Even though I often speak against him, I still remember him with love. So my heart longs for him. I will surely have mercy on him," says the LORD.
"Set up road signs. Put up guideposts. Pay attention to the highway, the road you traveled. Come back, young Israel. Come back to these towns of yours.
How long will you wander, unfaithful daughter? For the LORD has created something new on earth: a woman will protect a man."

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "When I bring them back from captivity, the people in the land of Judah and its towns will once again say: 'May the LORD bless you, home of righteousness, holy mountain.'
Judah and all its towns will live there together, the farmers and those who move about with their flocks.
For I will refresh the weary and satisfy everyone who is weak with sorrow."
At this I woke up and looked around. My sleep had been pleasant.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will fill the land of Israel and Judah with people and animals.
Just as I watched over them to uproot and tear down, to overthrow, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant," says the LORD.
"In those days people will no longer say, 'The parents have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'
Instead, each person will die for their own sin. Whoever eats sour grapes, their own teeth will be set on edge.
Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and the people of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt. They broke that covenant, even though I was like a husband to them," says the LORD.

"But this is the covenant I will make with the people of Israel after those days," says the LORD: "I will put my law inside them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

No longer will they need to teach their neighbors or their relatives, saying, 'Know the LORD,' because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest," says the LORD. "For I will forgive their sin, and I will never again remember their wrongs."
This is what the LORD says, he who gives the sun to light the day and sets the moon and stars to light the night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is his name:
"If these laws of nature ever disappear from my sight," says the LORD, "then Israel's descendants will stop being a nation before me forever."

This is what the LORD says: "If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be explored, then I will reject all of Israel's descendants for everything they have done," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when this city will be rebuilt for the LORD, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will stretch from there straight to the hill of Gareb and then turn toward Goah.

The whole valley where dead bodies and ashes are thrown, and all the fields as far as the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to the LORD. The city will never again be uprooted or torn down."
